ODesign.claim: Do not add review/navigation affordances unless their scope and interaction are consistent with the user's mental model.
ODesign.conditions: Section-local answer summaries looked interactive and behaved inconsistently across page structures.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: The feature did not meet the assumed need and created confusion.

ODesign.claim: Removal is a testable design intervention; validate it with a stated hypothesis and multiple guardrail metrics.
ODesign.conditions: The team did not know whether removing smart answers would harm completion.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Live-service before/after measurement.

ODesign.claim: Place review at the natural commitment boundary and allow correction before submission.
ODesign.conditions: Users expected to review the whole application rather than section-local summaries.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Prototype testing plus satisfaction-survey feedback.

ODesign.claim: Optional questions are not free: each adds interpretation and decision cost.
ODesign.conditions: A form presented many optional fields without a clear information hierarchy.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Users understood and completed the section faster.

ODesign.claim: A smaller, explicit question set can improve both user effort and downstream operational quality.
ODesign.conditions: The education section was slow and confusing.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Live completion-time and processing-quality data.

ODesign.claim: Flow polish cannot compensate for an intrinsically burdensome information demand.
ODesign.conditions: Employment questions added about 14 minutes and required hard-to-retrieve dates and payslips.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Completion time stayed the same; only the number of steps decreased slightly.

ODesign.claim: Escalate unresolved UX friction to policy, data, and operational-process redesign.
ODesign.conditions: A presentational redesign failed to reduce completion time.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Re-test completion time, abandonment, data completeness, and manual follow-up after implementation.

ODesign.claim: Support discoverability and support routing must be designed as one end-to-end service.
ODesign.conditions: A helpline was behind a disclosure and pointed to technical support although users needed eligibility help.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Calls were transferred because the support destination did not match the user need.

ODesign.claim: Do not equate shipping help content with a successful outcome; retain an inconclusive or failed result until metrics improve.
ODesign.conditions: The team introduced contextual links and a help guide.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Post-release completion-rate monitoring.

ODesign.claim: A good service distinguishes successful completion from a correct early exit.
ODesign.conditions: Users told they might not be entitled could only continue into a lengthy application.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Measure reason-coded exits separately from harmful abandonment.

ODesign.claim: Progress UI must answer a demonstrated question and match expected interaction.
ODesign.conditions: Users either did not notice the indicator or expected it to support navigation; some were intimidated by the section count.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Completion and time were unchanged.

ODesign.claim: A simpler system with fewer misleading components can be a successful design outcome.
ODesign.conditions: A progress component consumed attention without meeting the user need.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Live guardrail metrics and follow-up feedback.

ODesign.claim: Safety-critical continuous controls require immediate, perceivable state and mode feedback; visual-only controls may be inadequate.
ODesign.conditions: Ship thrust was controlled through touch-screen throttles that could be independently ganged or unganged.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: The interface increased the likelihood of operator errors contributing to a fatal collision.

ODesign.claim: Transfer of authority must be explicit, acknowledged, visible to all affected operators, and reversible.
ODesign.conditions: In backup manual mode another station could take steering without acknowledgement.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Control and mode changed in less than a second while operators perceived a system malfunction.

ODesign.claim: Match the control modality to the physical continuity, risk, and feedback needs of the task.
ODesign.conditions: Touch controls provided less direction, force, and gang-state feedback than mechanical throttles.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Conformance to ASTM F1166 plus representative bridge simulation.

ODesign.claim: A UI is not operationally complete until procedures and training cover normal, transfer, exception, and recovery states.
ODesign.conditions: Written procedures omitted transfer and ganging steps, and training had no standard for them.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Procedure traceability and observed proficiency tests.

ODesign.claim: Validation needs layered methods and performance evidence, not checklist-only approval.
ODesign.conditions: A single heuristic review cannot prove safe performance.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: The published EUP protocol itself specifies the independent validation method.

ODesign.claim: Workarounds are evidence of a system-work mismatch and should trigger root-cause analysis, not normalization.
ODesign.conditions: EHR workflows did not adequately support clinical cognitive work and flexible task sequencing.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Information quality, workload, and patient-safety risks increased.

ODesign.claim: Derive functions from observed goals, coordination, variability, and workload rather than from database structure.
ODesign.conditions: Billing-centred EHR design conflicted with clinician-centred goals.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: SME correction, interdisciplinary review, iterative diagrams, and published-evidence convergence.

ODesign.claim: Pair quantitative behaviour with qualitative explanation before prioritising UX changes.
ODesign.conditions: Analytics showed what visitors did but not why.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Cross-source convergence and post-change metric monitoring.

ODesign.claim: Accessibility validation must include representative users and their actual assistive technologies.
ODesign.conditions: Conformance checks alone did not reveal lived navigation problems.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Participant study with disability-community partnership.

ODesign.claim: Launch is a measurement point; sustained success requires an evidence-backed improvement backlog.
ODesign.conditions: USA.gov and USAGov en Español needed improved discoverability and task coverage.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Usability tests, visitor feedback, click data, and outcome trends.

ODesign.claim: Multilingual UX requires managed terminology, content governance, testing, and support—not literal string substitution.
ODesign.conditions: English-only or ad-hoc translation limited access and created inconsistent support.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Language-specific content review and representative-user task testing.

ODesign.claim: Treat the design system as a governed product with research, accessibility, release notes, and contribution loops.
ODesign.conditions: Service teams otherwise recreate common components and repeat solved accessibility work.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Component research, accessibility testing, versioned releases, and cross-service adoption evidence.

ODesign.claim: For civic and high-stakes systems, certify observable task performance across diverse users rather than visual conformance alone.
ODesign.conditions: General or low-level design prescriptions did not reliably prevent voter errors or exclusion.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Qualification/certification testing against complete user-related functional requirements.

ODesign.claim: Model the full service and its support ecosystem before optimising a single interface.
ODesign.conditions: Claimant needs and service operations cross digital and assisted channels.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: End-to-end journey and operational-service assessment.

ODesign.claim: Scale validation fidelity, scenario realism, and independence with consequence severity.
ODesign.conditions: Method selection can under-test complex or safety-critical work.
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Risk-based selection of observation, walkthrough, simulation, expert review, and summative tests.

ODesign.claim: The proposed AI capability solves a demonstrated need better than the baseline.
ODesign.conditions: Before selecting an AI feature or drawing a screen
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: A visually attractive AI feature is built without a validated user problem.

ODesign.claim: Optimization improves the user outcome without breaching guardrails.
ODesign.conditions: When defining AI success
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: The system maximizes clicks, speed, or model score while degrading trust, safety, or task completion.

ODesign.claim: The corpus grows by distinct reusable knowledge rather than paraphrase volume.
ODesign.conditions: Before registering generated UI/UX knowledge
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Requested counts are met by changing labels, roles, or proficiency levels.

ODesign.claim: The declared scope reaches an evidenced saturation point.
ODesign.conditions: Before declaring UI/UX research complete
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Research stops when an arbitrary target count is reached.

ODesign.claim: Registered, validated, promoted, and merged counts are equal for the promoted set.
ODesign.conditions: Before moving candidate UI/UX knowledge into the official corpus
ODesign.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Candidate creation or local validation is reported as learning completion.

ODesign.claim: Explore problems and alternatives broadly before converging on a defined brief and validated delivery.
ODesign.conditions: Design tasks with uncertain framing or multiple plausible solutions.
ODesign.exceptions: The framework page states CC BY 4.0; verify exact reused assets separately.
counterexamples: The first plausible result is accepted without discovery or alternative comparison.

ODesign.claim: Ground decisions in users, tasks, environments, and iterative evaluation throughout the lifecycle.
ODesign.conditions: Interactive products, services, controls, displays, and web experiences.
ODesign.exceptions: The full standard is licensed and must not be copied without rights.
counterexamples: Aesthetic preference substitutes for observed context and measured usability.

ODesign.claim: Size, contrast, spacing, alignment, and typography must express priority and reading order rather than decorate.
ODesign.conditions: Interfaces, advertisements, reports, packaging, signage, and publications.
ODesign.exceptions: Retain attribution and verify page terms before redistribution.
counterexamples: Every element competes equally or color alone carries meaning.

ODesign.claim: Physical-product design must jointly resolve appearance, functionality, manufacturability, and lasting user value.
ODesign.conditions: Mass-produced devices, appliances, tools, furniture, packaging, and controls.
procedure: Validate safety, manufacture, maintenance, and end-of-life
ODesign.exceptions: Do not reproduce protected imagery or extended source text.
counterexamples: A concept render is accepted despite unsafe ergonomics or no manufacturing route.

ODesign.claim: Physical controls, displays, sound, haptics, and companion interfaces must share one consistent state machine.
ODesign.conditions: Appliances, vehicles, kiosks, wearables, instruments, and connected products.
ODesign.exceptions: Derived candidate requiring expert validation and licensed-standard review.
counterexamples: The display contradicts the physical control or provides no recoverable feedback.

ODesign.claim: Web design must preserve perceivability, operability, understandability, and robustness as testable requirements.
ODesign.conditions: Web pages, applications, interactive documents, and embedded web views.
procedure: Meet contrast, target-size, input, and reflow rules
ODesign.exceptions: Preserve the standard version and exact criterion locator.
counterexamples: A polished page is promoted while keyboard, reflow, focus, alternatives, or target size fails.

ODesign.claim: Objective advertising claims and comparisons require documentary evidence and visible, understandable qualifications.
ODesign.conditions: Display, print, video, social, landing-page, environmental, and comparative advertising.
ODesign.exceptions: Market-specific legal review remains required.
counterexamples: Headline, imagery, or disclaimer creates a stronger promise than evidence supports.

ODesign.claim: Publication layout must preserve headings, reading order, alternatives, table structure, language, metadata, and reflow.
ODesign.conditions: Reports, books, manuals, brochures, PDF, EPUB, and digital publications.
procedure: Test tags, alternatives, zoom, and reflow
ODesign.exceptions: Evaluate each technique against target format and WCAG version.
counterexamples: The page looks correct but is flattened or has broken reading order and tables.

ODesign.claim: Typography must be tested for audience, medium, distance, language, line length, spacing, and reading duration.
ODesign.conditions: Long-form print and digital publications, manuals, reports, and captions.
ODesign.exceptions: Print-specific claims require separate evidence.
counterexamples: A fashionable treatment reduces legibility, loses characters, or breaks on export.

ODesign.claim: Generative design should create an editable foundation, preserve human control, and support repeated refinement.
ODesign.conditions: Prompt-to-layout, prompt-to-prototype, prompt-to-code, and AI asset generation.
procedure: Expose layers, components, code, and tokens
ODesign.exceptions: Vendor philosophy is descriptive, not independent proof of quality.
counterexamples: The result is a flattened image or opaque code that cannot be safely refined.

ODesign.claim: Learn general design patterns and tool structure without retaining or reproducing customer-specific content, concepts, or sensitive data.
ODesign.conditions: Training, fine-tuning, retrieval, telemetry, and prompt-to-design services.
ODesign.exceptions: Vendor statements require independent technical verification.
counterexamples: Customer designs or ideas are reproduced across tenants or reused beyond declared purposes.

ODesign.claim: Generated assets require source-rights controls, prompt and output safeguards, and provenance transparency before commercial use.
ODesign.conditions: Image, illustration, texture, advertising, packaging, brand, and publication generation.
ODesign.exceptions: Vendor claims do not replace project-specific rights review.
counterexamples: A suitable-looking asset is treated as commercially safe without rights or similarity checks.

source_binding.locator: Approach to generative AI with Adobe Firefly

ODesign.claim: An agent-ready design system needs predictable foundations, composable components, proven patterns, machine-readable tokens, and accessible implementation guidance.
ODesign.conditions: AI-assisted UI generation that must remain consistent, brandable, accessible, and maintainable.
procedure: Preserve component internals and override points
ODesign.exceptions: Secondary summary only; bind the primary Astryx documentation and MIT license before activation.
counterexamples: The agent copies surface styling without component semantics, interaction contracts, or accessible behavior.

source_binding.locator: Astryx summary: foundations, components, patterns and agent-facing CLI/MCP

ODesign.claim: When generation becomes cheap, design quality shifts to problem framing, value selection, constraints, and evidence of usefulness rather than output volume.
ODesign.conditions: AI-generated products, interfaces, campaigns, and content where many plausible artifacts can be produced quickly.
procedure: Define the user and business problem
ODesign.exceptions: Discovery-level candidate; full article bytes and author argument must be reviewed before promotion.
counterexamples: Fast artifact generation is mistaken for solving a worthwhile problem.

source_binding.locator: AI가 다 만드는데, 왜 자꾸 기획을 말할까?

ODesign.claim: Above-average design depends on explicit comparative judgment: recognizing generic output, explaining why one alternative fits better, and recording the selection criteria.
ODesign.conditions: LLM-generated visual, product, web, advertising, and publication alternatives.
procedure: Generate more than one viable option
Validate with target users and experts
ODesign.exceptions: Treat as a practitioner hypothesis until full text and independent evidence are reviewed.
counterexamples: The first polished-looking output is accepted because no decision criteria or comparative review exists.

ODesign.claim: Before inventing a new UI solution, retrieve applicable system components and established interaction patterns, then generate only the unresolved portion.
ODesign.conditions: Design-system-backed UI creation, redesign, and partial regeneration.
procedure: Generate and label only the gap
ODesign.exceptions: Do not copy a referenced design merely because it was retrieved; rights and project fitness remain separate gates.
counterexamples: The model hallucinates a novel component while an approved accessible component or pattern already exists.

source_binding.locator: AI에게 디자인을 지어내지 말고 찾아 쓰라

ODesign.claim: AI may adapt an interface, but stable user expectations, safety-critical conventions, accessibility semantics, and recovery patterns remain constraints rather than expendable templates.
ODesign.conditions: Adaptive, conversational, generative, and personalized interfaces.
ODesign.exceptions: The source raises a design question; the operational claim requires full-text and empirical validation.
counterexamples: Personalization changes controls or navigation so aggressively that users cannot predict, recover, or transfer learning.

ODesign.claim: Code, motion, 3D, shaders, components, and runtime behavior are design materials whose intent and parameters must remain connected from exploration through implementation.
ODesign.conditions: Interactive prototypes and products combining UI, animation, spatial effects, code, and production assets.
procedure: Compare implementation against the design contract
ODesign.exceptions: Product-report claims must be checked against Figma primary documentation and actual runtime behavior.
counterexamples: A canvas mockup is approved while motion, state, performance, or generated code diverges during implementation.

ODesign.claim: AI design orchestration should separate model choice from artifact contracts, keep credentials and project history local where required, and export inspectable editable formats.
ODesign.conditions: Confidential or regulated design work using multiple cloud or local models.
procedure: Select an allowed provider or local model
Generate through a stable artifact schema
Sandbox preview and verify each export
ODesign.exceptions: Verify security, privacy, format fidelity, and license claims against the project repository and releases.
counterexamples: Switching models changes the artifact contract, leaks protected data, or produces unverified flattened exports.

source_binding.locator: Open CoDesign local-first, multi-provider, artifact and exporter architecture

ODesign.claim: AI-assisted commerce redesign must preserve product truth, information hierarchy, reusable structure, and measurable purchase-task performance rather than optimize visual novelty alone.
ODesign.conditions: Product-detail pages, commerce landing pages, catalog content, and AI-assisted redesign.
procedure: A/B test comprehension and purchase-task outcomes
ODesign.exceptions: Case-study discovery only; do not infer outcomes or reuse assets without full source and project rights.
counterexamples: AI-generated imagery or copy improves appearance while distorting the product, hiding conditions, or weakening decision-critical information.

ODesign.claim: Field research must bind the problem context, research questions, participant criteria, method, tasks, ethics, records, and planned synthesis before observation begins.
ODesign.conditions: Products and services whose real context, workarounds, environment, or user behavior is not adequately known.
procedure: State the problem context and hypotheses
Record consent, observations, and synthesis plan
ODesign.exceptions: Validate the method against primary research ethics and UX research references before activation.
counterexamples: Unstructured conversations are treated as representative user evidence without recruitment, context, consent, or traceable notes.

ODesign.claim: A journey map is evidence-bound only when its actor, goal, lifecycle scope, touchpoints, actions, emotions, pain points, and opportunities trace to research.
ODesign.conditions: Multi-step services and cross-channel experiences involving several touchpoints, owners, or handoffs.
procedure: Define the goal and journey boundary
Attach evidence for pain and emotion
ODesign.exceptions: Templates and illustrations may have separate rights; retain only the method candidate.
counterexamples: A fictional journey generated from assumptions is presented as user research.

ODesign.claim: Prototype fidelity must match the question being tested, and usability evidence must come from representative users performing defined tasks.
ODesign.conditions: Flows, controls, navigation, information architecture, and interaction concepts before production release.
ODesign.exceptions: Introductory secondary material; triangulate with a primary usability-testing standard.
counterexamples: Stakeholder preference or a self-review of a polished prototype is labeled as usability validation.

source_binding.locator: 1-3 HCI와 UX 적용 기술—사용성 테스트와 프로토타이핑

ODesign.claim: AX is an operating-model redesign across value, decisions, process, roles, capability, governance, and learning—not merely insertion of an AI feature.
ODesign.conditions: Organization-wide AI transformation and AI-enabled service or product portfolios.
procedure: Assess data, process, people, and governance readiness
Pilot with adoption and risk controls
ODesign.exceptions: Broad synthesis candidate; each strategic claim needs primary organizational evidence.
counterexamples: Model deployment, automation count, or training completion is reported as transformation without sustained value or changed operations.

ODesign.claim: Prompt, sketch, or screenshot input should resolve to editable multi-screen structure and inspectable frontend code with explicit interaction links.
ODesign.conditions: AI-assisted wireframing, interface generation, prototyping, and design-to-code workflows.
ODesign.exceptions: Confirm capabilities and limits against current Google Stitch documentation and an actual export test.
counterexamples: The tool returns a convincing screenshot with no structure, interaction lineage, or maintainable implementation.

source_binding.locator: Google Stitch prompt/sketch/screenshot to editable UI and code

ODesign.claim: Portable agent design context must carry both machine-readable decisions and human-readable rationale, including roles, states, constraints, responsive behavior, and prohibited choices.
ODesign.conditions: Cross-tool design systems consumed by design and coding agents.
procedure: Test the same context across tools
ODesign.exceptions: Bind Atlassian's primary report and license; record token and latency tradeoffs rather than treating portability as free.
counterexamples: A palette and type list is called a design system while intent, state, behavior, and guardrails are absent.

ODesign.claim: Reverse-engineering a design system requires computed structure, responsive behavior, interaction states, motion, semantics, accessibility, and cross-page consistency—not color and spacing extraction alone.
ODesign.conditions: Migrating, auditing, learning from, or reproducing an authorized existing web design system.
ODesign.exceptions: Extraction does not grant reuse rights; verify the project code, license, robots policy, and target-site authorization.
counterexamples: A single screenshot or CSS scrape is generalized into a complete design system and applied without rights or behavioral evidence.

ODesign.claim: AX metrics must distinguish activity, adoption, operational performance, user outcome, business value, risk, and learning quality.
ODesign.conditions: AI-transformation portfolios, AI-enabled product programs, and organization-level change governance.
procedure: Stop or redesign when outcomes do not improve
ODesign.exceptions: Practitioner hypothesis; validate metric definitions against the target organization and independent evidence.
counterexamples: Automation counts, model calls, or course completion rise while user outcomes, process quality, risk, or business value deteriorate.

OUI.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Only the end-user happy path is designed.

OUI.claim: Registered, validated, promoted, and merged counts are equal for the promoted set.
OUI.conditions: Before moving candidate UI/UX knowledge into the official corpus
OUI.exceptions: Do not generalize beyond the stated context without a new reproduction.
counterexamples: Candidate creation or local validation is reported as learning completion.

OUI.claim: Size, contrast, spacing, alignment, and typography must express priority and reading order rather than decorate.
OUI.conditions: Interfaces, advertisements, reports, packaging, signage, and publications.
OUI.exceptions: Retain attribution and verify page terms before redistribution.
counterexamples: Every element competes equally or color alone carries meaning.

OUI.claim: Physical controls, displays, sound, haptics, and companion interfaces must share one consistent state machine.
OUI.conditions: Appliances, vehicles, kiosks, wearables, instruments, and connected products.
OUI.exceptions: Derived candidate requiring expert validation and licensed-standard review.
counterexamples: The display contradicts the physical control or provides no recoverable feedback.

OUI.claim: Web design must preserve perceivability, operability, understandability, and robustness as testable requirements.
OUI.conditions: Web pages, applications, interactive documents, and embedded web views.
procedure: Meet contrast, target-size, input, and reflow rules
OUI.exceptions: Preserve the standard version and exact criterion locator.
counterexamples: A polished page is promoted while keyboard, reflow, focus, alternatives, or target size fails.

OUI.claim: Publication layout must preserve headings, reading order, alternatives, table structure, language, metadata, and reflow.
OUI.conditions: Reports, books, manuals, brochures, PDF, EPUB, and digital publications.
procedure: Test tags, alternatives, zoom, and reflow
OUI.exceptions: Evaluate each technique against target format and WCAG version.
counterexamples: The page looks correct but is flattened or has broken reading order and tables.

OUI.claim: Typography must be tested for audience, medium, distance, language, line length, spacing, and reading duration.
OUI.conditions: Long-form print and digital publications, manuals, reports, and captions.
OUI.exceptions: Print-specific claims require separate evidence.
counterexamples: A fashionable treatment reduces legibility, loses characters, or breaks on export.

OUI.claim: Generative design should create an editable foundation, preserve human control, and support repeated refinement.
OUI.conditions: Prompt-to-layout, prompt-to-prototype, prompt-to-code, and AI asset generation.
procedure: Expose layers, components, code, and tokens
OUI.exceptions: Vendor philosophy is descriptive, not independent proof of quality.
counterexamples: The result is a flattened image or opaque code that cannot be safely refined.

OUI.claim: Learn general design patterns and tool structure without retaining or reproducing customer-specific content, concepts, or sensitive data.
OUI.conditions: Training, fine-tuning, retrieval, telemetry, and prompt-to-design services.
OUI.exceptions: Vendor statements require independent technical verification.
counterexamples: Customer designs or ideas are reproduced across tenants or reused beyond declared purposes.

OUI.claim: Generated assets require source-rights controls, prompt and output safeguards, and provenance transparency before commercial use.
OUI.conditions: Image, illustration, texture, advertising, packaging, brand, and publication generation.
OUI.exceptions: Vendor claims do not replace project-specific rights review.
counterexamples: A suitable-looking asset is treated as commercially safe without rights or similarity checks.

source_binding.locator: Approach to generative AI with Adobe Firefly

OUI.claim: An agent-ready design system needs predictable foundations, composable components, proven patterns, machine-readable tokens, and accessible implementation guidance.
OUI.conditions: AI-assisted UI generation that must remain consistent, brandable, accessible, and maintainable.
procedure: Preserve component internals and override points
OUI.exceptions: Secondary summary only; bind the primary Astryx documentation and MIT license before activation.
counterexamples: The agent copies surface styling without component semantics, interaction contracts, or accessible behavior.

source_binding.locator: Astryx summary: foundations, components, patterns and agent-facing CLI/MCP

OUI.claim: Before inventing a new UI solution, retrieve applicable system components and established interaction patterns, then generate only the unresolved portion.
OUI.conditions: Design-system-backed UI creation, redesign, and partial regeneration.
procedure: Generate and label only the gap
OUI.exceptions: Do not copy a referenced design merely because it was retrieved; rights and project fitness remain separate gates.
counterexamples: The model hallucinates a novel component while an approved accessible component or pattern already exists.

source_binding.locator: AI에게 디자인을 지어내지 말고 찾아 쓰라

OUI.claim: AI may adapt an interface, but stable user expectations, safety-critical conventions, accessibility semantics, and recovery patterns remain constraints rather than expendable templates.
OUI.conditions: Adaptive, conversational, generative, and personalized interfaces.
OUI.exceptions: The source raises a design question; the operational claim requires full-text and empirical validation.
counterexamples: Personalization changes controls or navigation so aggressively that users cannot predict, recover, or transfer learning.

OUI.claim: Code, motion, 3D, shaders, components, and runtime behavior are design materials whose intent and parameters must remain connected from exploration through implementation.
OUI.conditions: Interactive prototypes and products combining UI, animation, spatial effects, code, and production assets.
procedure: Compare implementation against the design contract
OUI.exceptions: Product-report claims must be checked against Figma primary documentation and actual runtime behavior.
counterexamples: A canvas mockup is approved while motion, state, performance, or generated code diverges during implementation.

OUI.claim: AI design orchestration should separate model choice from artifact contracts, keep credentials and project history local where required, and export inspectable editable formats.
OUI.conditions: Confidential or regulated design work using multiple cloud or local models.
procedure: Select an allowed provider or local model
Generate through a stable artifact schema
Sandbox preview and verify each export
OUI.exceptions: Verify security, privacy, format fidelity, and license claims against the project repository and releases.
counterexamples: Switching models changes the artifact contract, leaks protected data, or produces unverified flattened exports.

source_binding.locator: Open CoDesign local-first, multi-provider, artifact and exporter architecture

OUI.claim: AI-assisted commerce redesign must preserve product truth, information hierarchy, reusable structure, and measurable purchase-task performance rather than optimize visual novelty alone.
OUI.conditions: Product-detail pages, commerce landing pages, catalog content, and AI-assisted redesign.
procedure: A/B test comprehension and purchase-task outcomes
OUI.exceptions: Case-study discovery only; do not infer outcomes or reuse assets without full source and project rights.
counterexamples: AI-generated imagery or copy improves appearance while distorting the product, hiding conditions, or weakening decision-critical information.

OUI.claim: Prototype fidelity must match the question being tested, and usability evidence must come from representative users performing defined tasks.
OUI.conditions: Flows, controls, navigation, information architecture, and interaction concepts before production release.
OUI.exceptions: Introductory secondary material; triangulate with a primary usability-testing standard.
counterexamples: Stakeholder preference or a self-review of a polished prototype is labeled as usability validation.

source_binding.locator: 1-3 HCI와 UX 적용 기술—사용성 테스트와 프로토타이핑

OUI.claim: Accessibility validation requires criterion-based automated checks plus keyboard, screen-reader, zoom/reflow, focus, and human task testing.
OUI.conditions: Web applications, responsive interfaces, and digital publications.
procedure: Pin the target WCAG version and level
Test screen-reader output and focus order
Review failures with disabled users or qualified experts
OUI.exceptions: The pinned W3C WCAG version remains authoritative where this secondary guide differs.
counterexamples: A single automated score is accepted as proof that the experience is accessible.

OUI.claim: Prompt, sketch, or screenshot input should resolve to editable multi-screen structure and inspectable frontend code with explicit interaction links.
OUI.conditions: AI-assisted wireframing, interface generation, prototyping, and design-to-code workflows.
OUI.exceptions: Confirm capabilities and limits against current Google Stitch documentation and an actual export test.
counterexamples: The tool returns a convincing screenshot with no structure, interaction lineage, or maintainable implementation.

source_binding.locator: Google Stitch prompt/sketch/screenshot to editable UI and code

OUI.claim: Portable agent design context must carry both machine-readable decisions and human-readable rationale, including roles, states, constraints, responsive behavior, and prohibited choices.
OUI.conditions: Cross-tool design systems consumed by design and coding agents.
procedure: Test the same context across tools
OUI.exceptions: Bind Atlassian's primary report and license; record token and latency tradeoffs rather than treating portability as free.
counterexamples: A palette and type list is called a design system while intent, state, behavior, and guardrails are absent.

OUI.claim: Reverse-engineering a design system requires computed structure, responsive behavior, interaction states, motion, semantics, accessibility, and cross-page consistency—not color and spacing extraction alone.
OUI.conditions: Migrating, auditing, learning from, or reproducing an authorized existing web design system.
OUI.exceptions: Extraction does not grant reuse rights; verify the project code, license, robots policy, and target-site authorization.
counterexamples: A single screenshot or CSS scrape is generalized into a complete design system and applied without rights or behavioral evidence.
